packages.name: falcon
packages.doc:
Package falcon is a fast Go web framework for structured code. Every handler returns a response, every API response has the same shape, and every error takes the same path, so your frontend never has to guess what it's getting. - One response shape: API responses are always {success, message, details, code}. Anything else, like HTML or a file, has to come from a named helper. - Handlers must return: a handler that returns nil gets a logged 500, not a silent empty 200. - One error path: return c.Error(err) works everywhere, and details stay hidden from clients unless you turn on debug mode. - Mistakes show up at startup: conflicting routes and malformed patterns panic with a message naming the problem. - Fast: zero allocations when routing, and in our benchmarks faster than Gin and Echo on realistic API requests, with the least memory per request. # Installation Falcon requires Go 1.27 or newer. go get github.com/ascendingheavens/falcon # Getting started package main import ( "log" falcon "github.com/ascendingheavens/falcon" "github.com/ascendingheavens/falcon/middleware" ) func main() { app := falcon.New() app.Use(middleware.Logger()) app.Use(middleware.Recovery()) app.GET("/users/:id", func(c *falcon.Context) *falcon.Response { return c.OK("User found", map[string]string{"id": c.Param("id")}) }) if err := app.Start(":8080"); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } } A request to /users/42 returns: {"success":true,"message":"User found","details":{"id":"42"},"code":200} # Responses Handlers return a *Response. It only describes what to send: Falcon writes it after the handler and all middleware have returned, so middleware can still change it on the way out. return c.OK("User found", user) // 200 return c.Created("User created", user) // 201 return c.Error(err) // The status for that error, see Errors return c.ErrorJSON("Not allowed", nil, 403) // A failure with the code you choose Anything that isn't the JSON envelope has a named helper: return c.String(200, "plain text") return c.HTML(200, "

Hello

") return c.Render(200, "users/show.html", user) // A template, see Templates return c.File("./reports/latest.pdf") // With range requests and caching return c.Stream(200, "text/csv", reader) // Without holding it in memory return c.Redirect(302, "/login") return c.NoContent() // 204 # Errors c.Error turns any error into a response. Unknown errors become a generic 500: the real error is logged, and the client only sees it in debug mode. user, err := repo.Find(id) if err != nil { return c.Error(err) } return c.OK("User found", user) Map your own errors to responses in one place with [WithErrorMapper], and use [NewHTTPError] for errors that already know their status: return c.Error(falcon.NewHTTPError(403, "You can't edit this post")) # Binding and validation type CreateUserRequest struct { Name string `json:"name" validate:"required,min=2"` Email string `json:"email" validate:"required,email"` } func CreateUser(c *falcon.Context) *falcon.Response { var req CreateUserRequest if err := c.BindJSON(&req); err != nil { return c.Error(err) // 400 for a malformed body, 413 if it's too large } if err := c.Validate(&req); err != nil { return c.Error(err) // 422 listing the invalid fields, by their json names } return c.Created("User created", req) } # Templates renderer, err := falcon.NewTemplateRenderer("views", nil) if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } app.SetRenderer(renderer) Templates are named by their path inside the folder, such as "users/show.html". Files in the layouts/ and partials/ folders are shared, and each page can define its own blocks. Output is escaped automatically, and a failing template gives a clean 500 instead of half a page. Use [NewTemplateRendererFS] with embed.FS to ship templates inside your binary. # Routing app.GET("/users", listUsers) app.GET("/users/me", currentUser) // Static segments beat params app.GET("/users/:id", getUser) // c.Param("id") app.GET("/static/*filepath", serveFile) // c.Param("filepath") is the rest of the path v1 := app.Group("/api/v1") v1.POST("/users", createUser) Falcon answers unknown paths with a 404 and the wrong method with a 405 and an Allow header, redirects a trailing slash to the route that exists, and handles HEAD and OPTIONS. # Middleware app.Use(middleware.Logger()) // Every request app.UseIf(AuthMiddleware(), "/api/v1/*", "/admin/*") // Only these routes app.UseIfNot(AuthMiddleware(), "/health", "/auth/*") // Every route except these The order is fixed, outermost first: global, then UseIf and UseIfNot, then group, then the handler. Patterns match whole segments, so "/api/*" matches "/api/users" but not "/apiary". The built-in middleware is in the middleware package. # Running the server [Server.Start], [Server.StartTLS] and [Server.StartAutoTLS] block until the server stops and return an error rather than exiting your program. For a graceful shutdown, call [Server.Shutdown] and wait for it to return before exiting.

packages.name: middleware
packages.doc:
Package middleware provides Falcon's built-in middleware.

	app.Use(middleware.Logger())
	app.Use(middleware.Recovery())
	app.Use(middleware.CORS())
	app.Use(middleware.RateLimit(100, time.Minute))

	app.UseIf(middleware.RateLimit(5, time.Minute), "/auth/login")
	app.UseIf(middleware.ConcurrencyLimit(10), "/reports/*")

A middleware wraps a handler. Code after next(c) can read and change the response:

	func Timing() middleware.Middleware {
		return func(next server.HandlerFunc) server.HandlerFunc {
			return func(c *server.Context) *server.Response {
				start := time.Now()
				resp := next(c)
				c.Writer.Header().Set("X-Duration", time.Since(start).String())
				return resp
			}
		}
	}

# CORS

Register CORS with app.Use, so that it can answer preflight requests, which only run
global middleware. [CORS] allows every origin without credentials. To allow cookies
across origins, list the origins with [CORSWithConfig].

# CSRF

[CSRF] expects a token in the X-CSRF-Token header or a csrf_token form field. Handlers
read it with c.Get("csrf_token"), to return it to a frontend or render it into a form.

# Rate limiting

[RateLimit] tells clients apart by their connection's IP address, never by a header a
client can forge. Clients over the limit get a 429 with a Retry-After header, and every
response carries RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset headers. Limits
are kept in memory, so with several instances of your app each one counts separately.
[ConcurrencyLimit] caps how many requests are handled at once.

packages.name: server
packages.doc:
Package server holds the types a Falcon handler works with: the [Context] for each
request, the [Response] it returns, errors, validation, templates and the router.

The falcon package makes the ones you use day to day available under the same names,
such as falcon.Context and falcon.Response, so most apps never import this package. It's
needed for [NewValidator], to build a custom validator that reports fields by their json
names, and when writing middleware outside the falcon package.

A Context is reused for later requests once its handler returns. A goroutine that
outlives the handler must use [Context.Copy].

types.name: ConditionalMiddleware
types.doc:
ConditionalMiddleware is an alias to middleware.ConditionalMiddleware,
which pairs a pattern (e.g., "/api/*") with a Middleware function.
types.code: type ConditionalMiddleware = middleware.ConditionalMiddleware

types.name: Context
types.doc:
Context is an alias to server.Context, which wraps the request and response
writer and provides convenience methods (params, body parsing, etc.).
types.code: type Context = server.Context

types.name: FieldError
types.doc: FieldError is an alias to server.FieldError, one invalid field in a ValidationError.
types.code: type FieldError = server.FieldError

types.name: Group
types.doc:
Group represents a collection of routes that share a common path prefix
and middleware stack. Useful for organizing related endpoints like `/api/v1/*`.

methods.name: DELETE
methods.doc:
DELETE registers a route with the HTTP DELETE method for this group.
The handler is invoked when a request matches the given path.

methods.name: GET
methods.doc:
GET registers a route with the HTTP GET method for this group.
The handler is invoked when a request matches the given path.

methods.name: Handle
methods.doc:
Handle registers a route for the group with a specific HTTP method and path.
It automatically prepends the group's prefix to the path. The group's middleware
applies to the route no matter whether it was added before or after.
methods.code: func (g *Group) Handle(method, path string, handler HandlerFunc)

methods.name: PATCH
methods.doc:
PATCH registers a route with the HTTP PATCH method for this group.
The handler is invoked when a request matches the given path.

methods.name: POST
methods.doc:
POST registers a route with the HTTP POST method for this group.
The handler is invoked when a request matches the given path.

methods.name: PUT
methods.doc:
PUT registers a route with the HTTP PUT method for this group.
The handler is invoked when a request matches the given path.

methods.name: Use
methods.doc:
Use registers a middleware for this specific group.
These middlewares are applied only to routes within the group,
in addition to any global middleware from the parent server.

types.name: HTTPError
types.doc:
HTTPError is an alias to server.HTTPError, an error that knows which
response it should become. Pass it to c.Error.
types.code: type HTTPError = server.HTTPError

types.name: Handler
types.doc:
Handler is a common interface implemented by both Server and Group.
It provides methods for registering middleware and defining routes
using standard HTTP methods. This allows groups and servers to be
used interchangeably when registering routes.

types.name: HandlerFunc
types.doc:
HandlerFunc is an alias to server.HandlerFunc, the function signature
that route handlers must implement. It takes a *Context and returns a *Response.
types.code: type HandlerFunc = server.HandlerFunc

types.name: Middleware
types.doc:
Middleware is an alias to middleware.Middleware, representing a function
that wraps and modifies a HandlerFunc, similar to how middleware works
in frameworks like Express or Fiber.
types.code: type Middleware = middleware.Middleware

types.name: Option
types.doc:
Option configures a Server. Pass options to New.
Example: app := falcon.New(falcon.WithDebug(), falcon.WithBodyLimit(1<<20))
types.code: type Option func(*Server)

types.name: Response
types.doc:
Response is an alias to server.Response, the unified return type
from every handler function. Encoded as JSON and written to the client.
types.code: type Response = server.Response

types.name: Server
types.doc:
Server is the main entry point for the Falcon framework.
It holds the router, global middlewares, and any conditional middlewares
that should be applied based on route patterns.

methods.name: DELETE
methods.doc:
DELETE registers a route with the HTTP DELETE method on the server.
The handler is invoked when a request matches the given path.

methods.name: GET
methods.doc:
GET registers a route with the HTTP GET method on the server.
The handler is invoked when a request matches the given path.

methods.name: Group
methods.doc:
Group represents a collection of routes sharing a common prefix
and middleware stack. Useful for organizing related endpoints.
Example: v1 := app.Group("/api/v1")

methods.name: Handle
methods.doc:
Handle registers a route with a specific HTTP method and path.
It panics if the route conflicts with one that is already registered.
methods.code: func (s *Server) Handle(method, path string, handler server.HandlerFunc)

methods.name: PATCH
methods.doc:
PATCH registers a route with the HTTP PATCH method on the server.
The handler is invoked when a request matches the given path.

methods.name: POST
methods.doc:
POST registers a route with the HTTP POST method on the server.
The handler is invoked when a request matches the given path.

methods.name: PUT
methods.doc:
PUT registers a route with the HTTP PUT method on the server.
The handler is invoked when a request matches the given path.

methods.name: SetRenderer
methods.doc:
SetRenderer sets the TemplateRenderer used by c.Render. Like middleware, it must be
set before the first request. With WithDebug, templates reload on every render.
Example:

	renderer, err := falcon.NewTemplateRenderer("views", nil)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	app.SetRenderer(renderer)

methods.name: Shutdown
methods.doc:
Shutdown stops the server gracefully: it stops accepting connections and waits for
the requests in progress to finish, or for ctx to end, whichever comes first.

Example:

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	err := app.Shutdown(ctx)

methods.name: Start
StartAutoTLS
methods.doc:
StartAutoTLS starts the server with automatic TLS certificate management using Let's Encrypt.
This method automatically obtains and renews TLS certificates for the specified domain
using the ACME protocol. The server will bind to port 443.
It blocks until the server stops, returning nil after a Shutdown and otherwise
the error that stopped it.

Parameters:
  - domain: The domain name for which to obtain certificates (e.g., "example.com")

The method sets up:
  - Automatic certificate cache in a local "certs" directory
  - Automatic acceptance of Let's Encrypt Terms of Service
  - Host whitelist policy for the specified domain
  - TLS configuration with automatic certificate retrieval

Requirements:
  - The server must be accessible from the internet on port 443
  - The domain must point to the server's IP address
  - Port 80 should also be available for ACME challenges (handled automatically by autocert)

Example:

	app := falcon.New()
	if err := app.StartAutoTLS("example.com"); err != nil { // Will serve HTTPS on port 443
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

methods.name: StartAutoTLSWithStarter
methods.doc:
StartAutoTLSWithStarter starts the server with automatic TLS certificate management
using a custom TLS starter. This method provides the same automatic certificate
functionality as StartAutoTLS but allows dependency injection of the server
startup mechanism, making it testable.

Parameters:
  - domain: The domain name for which to obtain certificates (e.g., "example.com")
  - starter: An implementation of TLSStarter interface that handles server startup

This method is primarily intended for testing purposes where you need to mock
the server startup behavior. For production use, prefer StartAutoTLS which
uses the server's own startup mechanism.

The method configures:
  - autocert.Manager with local certificate caching
  - Automatic TOS acceptance for Let's Encrypt
  - Host policy restricting certificates to the specified domain
  - HTTP server bound to port 443 with TLS configuration

Example:

	app := falcon.New()
	mockStarter := &MockTLSStarter{...}
	err := app.StartAutoTLSWithStarter("example.com", mockStarter)
methods.code: func (s *Server) StartAutoTLSWithStarter(domain string, starter TLSStarter) error

methods.name: StartTLS
methods.doc:
StartTLS starts the server with TLS using the provided certificate and key files.
The server will bind to the specified address and serve HTTPS traffic.
It blocks until the server stops, returning nil after a Shutdown and otherwise
the error that stopped it.

Parameters:
  - addr: The address to bind to (e.g., ":443", "localhost:8443")
  - certFile: Path to the TLS certificate file
  - keyFile: Path to the TLS private key file

Example:

	app := falcon.New()
	if err := app.StartTLS(":443", "/path/to/cert.pem", "/path/to/key.pem"); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
methods.code: func (s *Server) StartTLS(addr, certFile, keyFile string) error

methods.name: Use
methods.doc:
Use registers a global middleware that will run on every request, including
the ones no route matches. Middleware is executed in the order it is added,
and applies to every route no matter whether it was registered before or after.
Example:

	server.Use(middleware.CORS())

methods.name: UseIf
methods.doc:
UseIf registers a middleware that only runs on routes matching one of the patterns.
"/api/*" matches "/api" and everything below it, but not "/apiary"; a pattern with
no wildcard matches only the route with exactly that path. Patterns are resolved
once per route, so they cost nothing per request. They panic if malformed.
Requests no route matches, such as 404s, don't run conditional middleware.
Example: UseIf(AuthMiddleware(), "/api/v1/*", "/admin/*")

methods.name: UseIfNot
methods.doc:
UseIfNot registers a middleware that runs on every route except those matching one
of the patterns, which work as in UseIf.
Example: UseIfNot(AuthMiddleware(), "/health", "/auth/*")

types.name: TLSStarter
types.doc:
TLSStarter defines an interface for starting a TLS server.
Implementations should provide the startTLSServer method to handle
the server startup logic for HTTPS.

types.name: TemplateRenderer
types.doc:
TemplateRenderer is an alias for server.TemplateRenderer.
It is responsible for rendering HTML templates within Falcon.
types.code: type TemplateRenderer = server.TemplateRenderer

types.name: Timeouts
types.doc: Timeouts are the limits of the underlying http.Server. Zero means no limit.

types.name: ValidationError
types.doc: ValidationError is an alias to server.ValidationError, returned by c.Validate.
types.code: type ValidationError = server.ValidationError

types.name: CORSConfig
types.doc:
CORSConfig defines configuration for Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS).
Allows specifying which origins, headers, and methods are permitted.

types.name: CSRFConfig
types.doc: CSRFConfig defines configuration for CSRF protection middleware.
types.code:
type CSRFConfig struct {
	TokenHeader	string						// Header the client can send the token in
	TokenForm	string						// Form field the client can send the token in, for HTML forms
	TokenCookie	string						// Cookie name holding the value the token is derived from
	ContextKey	string						// Context key where handlers read the token to give to the client
	Expiry		time.Duration					// Cookie expiration duration
	Secret		[]byte						// HMAC secret. If empty a random one is generated, so set it when running several instances
	SkipMethods	[]string					// HTTP methods that don't require validation (safe methods)
	ErrorHandler	func(*server.Context, error) *server.Response	// Optional custom error handler
	CookieSecure	bool						// Whether the cookie is Secure
	CookieHTTPOnly	bool						// Whether the cookie is HttpOnly
	CookieSameSite	http.SameSite					// The cookie's SameSite mode. Defaults to Lax
}

types.name: ConditionalMiddleware

methods.name: AppliesTo
methods.doc: AppliesTo reports whether the middleware should wrap the route with this path.

types.name: Middleware
types.doc:
Middleware defines the function signature for all middleware in Falcon.
A middleware wraps a HandlerFunc, allowing pre- or post-processing of requests.
Examples include logging, authentication, profiling, or panic recovery.
types.code: type Middleware func(server.HandlerFunc) server.HandlerFunc

types.name: RateLimitConfig
types.doc:
RateLimitConfig defines configuration for the rate limiting middleware.
Each client may make Limit requests every Per, and up to Burst of them at once.

types.name: ValidationConfig
types.doc:
ValidationConfig holds configuration for the validation middleware.
Allows injecting a custom validator instance (from go-playground/validator/v10).

types.name: Context
types.doc:
Context wraps http.ResponseWriter and *http.Request, providing
convenience access to route parameters and helper methods in the future.
Fields:
  - Writer: the http.ResponseWriter to write responses.
  - Request: the incoming HTTP request.
  - Params: the path parameters extracted from the route (e.g., ":id").

Contexts are pooled and reused once the handler returns. A goroutine that outlives
the handler must use Copy, not the Context it was given.

methods.name: Bind
BindForm
methods.doc:
BindForm parses form data and binds it to a map
Takes only the first value for each key

methods.name: BindFormAll
methods.doc: BindFormAll parses URL-encoded form data and returns all values in a url.Values map.

methods.name: BindJSON
methods.doc:
BindJSON enforces JSON Content-Type and decodes into dest.
If binding fails it returns an *HTTPError, like Bind.

methods.name: BindXML
methods.doc:
BindXML enforces XML Content-Type and decodes into dest.
If binding fails it returns an *HTTPError, like Bind.

methods.name: Blob
methods.doc:
Blob returns a response with raw binary data and the given Content-Type.
Example: return c.Blob(200, data, "image/png")
methods.code: func (c *Context) Blob(code int, data []byte, contentType string) *Response

methods.name: Copy
methods.doc:
Copy returns a Context that stays valid after the handler returns, for use in goroutines:

	cp := c.Copy()
	go audit(cp.Param("id"), cp.Get("user"))

The copy can't respond to the client: anything written to it is discarded.
Its Request is shared, and net/http closes the request's Body and cancels its
context once the handler returns, so read what you need from those beforehand.

methods.name: Created
methods.doc:
Created returns a successful 201 response.
Example: return c.Created("User created", user)

methods.name: Error
ErrorJSON
methods.doc: ErrorJSON returns a failure response. To turn an existing error into a response, use Error.
methods.code: func (c *Context) ErrorJSON(message string, details any, code int) *Response

methods.name: File
methods.doc:
File returns a response that serves a file from disk, with support for range
requests and caching. If the file doesn't exist, it returns a 404 instead.
The path is used as given, so never build it directly from user input.
Example: return c.File("./reports/latest.pdf")

methods.name: FormFile
methods.doc:
FormFile retrieves the file from a multipart form.
It returns the first file for the provided form key.
A request over the server's body limit gives an error that c.Error turns into a 413;
raise the limit with falcon.WithBodyLimit if you accept large uploads.
Example: <input type="file" name="avatar" /> -> c.FormFile("avatar")

methods.name: FormValue
methods.doc:
FormValue returns the first value for the named component of the POST or PUT request body.
It calls ParseMultipartForm and ParseForm if necessary. It can't report errors, so a
request over the server's body limit gives "".
Example: <input type="text" name="username" /> -> c.FormValue("username")

methods.name: Get
methods.doc:
Get retrieves a value from the Context by key.
Returns nil if the key does not exist.
Example: user := c.Get("user")

methods.name: HTML
methods.doc:
HTML returns an HTML response. Example: return c.HTML(200, "

Hello

")

methods.name: JSON
methods.doc:
JSON returns a response with every field of the envelope given explicitly.
For the common cases see OK and Created for success, and Error for failure.
methods.code: func (c *Context) JSON(success bool, message string, details any, code int) *Response

methods.name: NoContent
methods.doc: NoContent returns a 204 response with no body.

methods.name: OK
methods.doc:
OK returns a successful 200 response.
Example: return c.OK("User found", user)

methods.name: Param
methods.doc:
Param returns the value of a path parameter by name.
Example: /users/:id -> c.Param("id") returns "123"

methods.name: PostFormValue
methods.doc:
PostFormValue is like FormValue but only reads the request body, ignoring the URL query.
Bodies that aren't forms, such as JSON, are left unread for the handler.

methods.name: Query
methods.doc:
Query returns the first value of a URL query parameter by key.
Example: /search?q=golang -> c.Query("q") returns "golang"

methods.name: QueryArray
methods.doc:
QueryArray returns all values for a query parameter key.
Example: /filter?tag=go&tag=web -> c.QueryArray("tag") returns []string{"go", "web"}

methods.name: Redirect
methods.doc:
Redirect returns an HTTP redirect to the specified location.
Example: return c.Redirect(302, "/login")

methods.name: Render
methods.doc:
Render returns a response with the named template rendered using the server's renderer,
set with app.SetRenderer. The page is rendered in full first, so a template that fails
halfway gives a clean 500 and never a partial page. In debug mode, templates are parsed
again on every call so that edits show up without a restart, and a template that no
longer parses gives a 500 with the reason until it's fixed.

Example: return c.Render(200, "users/show.html", user)
methods.code: func (c *Context) Render(code int, name string, data any) *Response

methods.name: Reset
methods.doc:
Reset prepares a pooled Context for a new request, keeping the Params capacity
so that later requests don't allocate. Passing nil clears it for return to the pool.

methods.name: Set
methods.doc:
Set stores a value in the Context under the specified key.
Example: c.Set("user", claims)

methods.name: SetValidator
methods.doc: SetValidator sets the validator c.Validate uses for this request.

methods.name: ShouldBind
methods.doc:
ShouldBind attempts to decode the request body into dest based on Content-Type
and returns the underlying error if it fails.

methods.name: ShouldBindForm
methods.doc: ShouldBindForm binds application/x-www-form-urlencoded form values into a struct.

methods.name: ShouldBindJSON
methods.doc: ShouldBindJSON decodes JSON without automatic error response.

methods.name: ShouldBindMultipart
methods.doc: ShouldBindMultipart binds multipart form to struct.

methods.name: ShouldBindXML
methods.doc: ShouldBindXML decodes XML without automatic error response.

methods.name: Stream
methods.doc:
Stream returns a response whose body is copied from r as it's sent, without holding
it all in memory. Use it for large or generated bodies, such as exports or proxying.
If r is an io.Closer it's closed afterwards, even if middleware replaced the response.
The server's write timeout doesn't apply to a stream.
Example: return c.Stream(200, "text/csv", exportReader)
methods.code: func (c *Context) Stream(code int, contentType string, r io.Reader) *Response

methods.name: String
methods.doc:
String returns a plain text response.
Example: return c.String(200, "Hello World")

methods.name: Validate
WriteResponse
methods.doc:
WriteResponse sends a Response to the client. The server calls it once the handler
and all middleware have returned. It does nothing if the handler took over the
Writer (c.Handled) or the response has already been written.

types.name: FieldError
types.doc: FieldError describes one invalid field in a request.

types.name: HTTPError
types.doc:
HTTPError is an error that knows which response it should become.
Message and Details are sent to the client. Err is the underlying cause: it's
logged on 5xx errors, and only sent to the client in debug mode.

Example: return c.Error(falcon.NewHTTPError(403, "You can't edit this post"))

methods.name: Error
methods.doc: Error implements the error interface.

methods.name: Unwrap
methods.doc: Unwrap returns the underlying cause, for errors.Is and errors.As.

types.name: HandlerFunc
types.doc:
HandlerFunc defines the signature for all route handlers in Falcon.
Every handler receives a pointer to a Context and returns a pointer to a Response.
The framework automatically writes the Response as JSON to the client.
types.code: type HandlerFunc func(c *Context) *Response

types.name: Param
types.doc: Param is a single path parameter extracted from a request path.

types.name: Params
types.doc:
Params holds the path parameters of a request, in the order they appear in the route.
A slice is used instead of a map because routes have few params: a short scan is
faster than a map lookup and a pooled slice doesn't allocate.

methods.name: Get
methods.doc: Get returns the value of the named parameter, or "" if it isn't present.

types.code: type Params []Param

types.name: Response
types.doc:
Response is the unified return type for all handlers in Falcon.
It is automatically serialized to JSON and written to the client.
Fields:
  - Success: indicates whether the request was successful.
  - Message: human-readable message describing the result.
  - Details: optional field containing extra data (any type).
  - Code: HTTP status code to be sent to the client. It's Required to have at least one Status code

A Response only describes what to send: the server writes it once the handler and
all middleware have returned, so middleware can still change it on the way out.
Anything other than this JSON shape (HTML, files, redirects...) can only come from
the helpers on Context, such as c.HTML or c.File, because raw can't be set from outside.

methods.name: ContentType
methods.doc:
ContentType returns the content type of a raw response. It's "" for the JSON
envelope, and for raw responses without a body or whose type comes from a file.

methods.name: IsRaw
methods.doc: IsRaw reports whether the response is sent as something other than the JSON envelope.

types.name: Route
types.doc:
Route represents a single registered route in the router.
It contains the HTTP method, the route path pattern, and the handler function.

types.name: Router
types.doc:
Router is an HTTP router backed by one radix tree per HTTP method. It supports
static segments, path parameters (/users/:id) and catch-alls (/static/*filepath).
Lookups don't allocate and their cost depends on the path, not the number of routes.

methods.name: AllowedMethods
methods.doc:
AllowedMethods returns the sorted methods a path can be requested with, or nil if
no route matches it. HEAD is included when GET is, and OPTIONS is always included,
because the server answers both automatically.

methods.name: FindHandler
methods.doc:
FindHandler attempts to match an incoming request (method + path)
against the registered routes and appends any path parameters to params.
It returns nil if no route matches, leaving params unchanged.
methods.code: func (r *Router) FindHandler(method, path string, params *Params) HandlerFunc

methods.name: Handle
methods.doc:
Handle registers a new route with a specific HTTP method, path, and handler.
It panics if the path doesn't start with "/" or conflicts with an existing route,
so mistakes surface at startup instead of on some later request.
The returned Route's Handler can be replaced until the router starts serving.
methods.code: func (r *Router) Handle(method, path string, handler HandlerFunc) *Route

methods.name: Routes
methods.doc: Routes returns every registered route.

types.name: Settings
types.doc: Settings holds the server-wide options the Context needs while handling a request.
types.code:
type Settings struct {
	Debug		bool				// Show error details to clients
	ErrorMapper	func(err error) *Response	// Turns application errors into responses, or returns nil to pass
	BodyLimit	int64				// Maximum size of a request body, in bytes
	MultipartMemory	int64				// Maximum bytes of a multipart form kept in memory, the rest goes to disk
	Renderer	*TemplateRenderer		// Renders templates for c.Render
}

types.name: TemplateRenderer
types.doc:
TemplateRenderer renders HTML templates. Output is always escaped by html/template. Every file with a .html, .tmpl or .gohtml extension is a template, named by its slash-separated path relative to the root, such as "users/show.html". Files under the top-level layouts/ and partials/ folders are shared with every other template. Everything else is a page, parsed separately, so that any number of pages can define the same block without overwriting each other: {{template "partials/nav.html" .}}{{template "content" .}} {{template "layouts/base.html" .}} {{define "content"}}

{{.Name}}

{{end}} It's safe for concurrent use.

methods.name: Render
methods.doc:
Render executes the named template and writes the output to w. Handlers should
use c.Render instead; this is for rendering elsewhere, such as into an email.
methods.code: func (tr *TemplateRenderer) Render(w io.Writer, name string, data any) error

types.name: ValidationError
types.doc:
ValidationError is returned by c.Validate when fields are invalid.
c.Error turns it into a 422 response whose details list the fields.

methods.name: Error
methods.doc: Error implements the error interface.

methods.name: Unwrap
methods.doc: Unwrap returns the original error from the validator.

functions.name: NewHTTPError
functions.doc:
NewHTTPError creates an error that c.Error turns into a response with this code and message.
Example: return c.Error(falcon.NewHTTPError(403, "You can't edit this post"))

functions.name: WithBodyLimit
functions.doc:
WithBodyLimit sets the maximum size of a request body in bytes, including file uploads.
Larger bodies get a 413. The default is 10MB, so raise it if you accept large uploads.

functions.name: WithDebug
functions.doc:
WithDebug makes error responses include the underlying error, which helps during
development but exposes internals. Never use it in production.

functions.name: WithErrorMapper
WithMultipartMemory
functions.doc:
WithMultipartMemory sets how many bytes of a multipart form are kept in memory;
the rest is stored in temporary files. The default is 32MB.

functions.name: WithTimeouts
functions.doc:
WithTimeouts replaces the server's timeouts. Any limit left at zero is turned off.
The defaults are 10s to read headers, 60s to read a request, 60s to write a
response, and 120s for an idle connection.

functions.name: New
functions.doc:
New creates a new Falcon Server instance with an empty router and middleware stack.
Example:

	server := falcon.New()
	server := falcon.New(falcon.WithDebug())

functions.name: NewTemplateRenderer
functions.doc:
NewTemplateRenderer parses every template (.html, .tmpl, .gohtml) under dir. Templates
are named by their path relative to dir, such as "users/show.html". Files under the
top-level layouts/ and partials/ folders are shared with every template.
functions.code: func NewTemplateRenderer(dir string, funcs template.FuncMap) (*TemplateRenderer, error)

functions.name: NewTemplateRendererFS
functions.doc:
NewTemplateRendererFS is like NewTemplateRenderer but reads templates from fsys, such
as an embed.FS, which ships them inside the binary.
functions.code: func NewTemplateRendererFS(fsys fs.FS, funcs template.FuncMap) (*TemplateRenderer, error)

functions.name: NewConditionalMiddleware
functions.doc:
NewConditionalMiddleware creates a ConditionalMiddleware. It panics on patterns that
couldn't match what they appear to mean, so the mistake shows up at startup.
functions.code: func NewConditionalMiddleware(mw Middleware, negate bool, patterns []string) ConditionalMiddleware

functions.name: CORS
functions.doc:
CORS returns a default CORS middleware using defaultCORSConfig.
It allows all origins, common HTTP methods, and standard headers, without credentials.
To allow cookies or Authorization across origins, list the origins with CORSWithConfig.

functions.name: CORSWithConfig
functions.doc:
CORSWithConfig returns a CORS middleware configured with the given CORSConfig.
Parameters:
  - cfg: custom CORS configuration (AllowOrigins, AllowMethods, AllowHeaders, AllowCredentials).

It panics if AllowOrigins contains "*" while AllowCredentials is set, because that
would let any website make logged-in requests on behalf of a user.

Behavior:
  - Sets `Vary: Origin`, so that caches keep responses for different origins apart.
  - Sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` to "*", or to the request origin if it's listed.
  - Sets `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` only if cfg.AllowCredentials is set.
  - Sets `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` and `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` on preflight.
  - Handles OPTIONS preflight requests with HTTP 204 and stops further processing.
  - Requests without an Origin header aren't cross-origin, and pass straight through.

functions.name: CSRF
functions.doc:
CSRF returns a middleware using the default CSRF configuration.
It validates incoming requests for unsafe methods and gives every request a token.

The secret is random, so tokens stop working on restart and aren't shared between
instances. Use CSRFWithConfig with a Secret if that matters.

functions.name: CSRFWithConfig
functions.doc:
CSRFWithConfig returns a CSRF middleware with a custom configuration.

Parameters:
  - cfg: CSRFConfig struct to override defaults (header, cookie, secret, expiry, etc.)

It works as a signed double submit: a cookie holds a random value, and an unsafe
request must send the HMAC of that value, in cfg.TokenHeader or the cfg.TokenForm form
field. Another site can make a browser send the cookie, but it can't read it or
compute the HMAC.

Handlers read the token to give to the client with c.Get(cfg.ContextKey), for example
from an endpoint the frontend calls first, or by rendering it into a form:

	<input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{.CSRFToken}}">

Behavior:
  - Skips validation for HTTP methods listed in cfg.SkipMethods.
  - Reads the token from the header, then from the form body. Never from a cookie: a
    browser attaches cookies to forged requests on its own, so they prove nothing. Never
    from the URL query either, where tokens leak through logs and Referer headers.
  - Validates the token against the cookie and the server-side secret.
  - Returns 403 Forbidden if the token or cookie is missing or the token is wrong
    (or calls cfg.ErrorHandler if defined).
  - Ensures a cookie is set and a token is in the context on every other request.

functions.name: ConcurrencyLimit
functions.doc:
ConcurrencyLimit returns a middleware that lets at most n requests be handled at once,
and answers any more with a 503 straight away instead of queueing them. Use it on slow
or expensive routes, such as reports or calls to other services.

It counts the time the handler and the middleware inside it run. The response is
written after that, so a long download from c.File or c.Stream doesn't hold a place.
Rejections aren't logged, because logging every one would add to the load at the
moment the server can least afford it.

Example: app.UseIf(middleware.ConcurrencyLimit(10), "/reports/*")

functions.name: JWTMiddleware
functions.doc:
JWTMiddleware returns a middleware that validates JWT tokens in the Authorization header.
The token must use the "Bearer " scheme, e.g. "Authorization: Bearer <token>".
It verifies the token using the provided HMAC secret.
If the token is invalid, missing, or has the wrong signing method, it returns a 401 Unauthorized response.
On success, the token claims are stored in the Context under the key "user" for access in handlers.

Example usage:

	app.Use(JWTMiddleware("supersecretkey"))

functions.name: Logger
functions.doc:
Logger returns a middleware that logs each request's method, path, status and duration
through the standard log package, which adds the date and time:

	2026/11/07 13:54:30 GET "/users/42" 200 (182.4µs)

functions.name: ProfilingMiddleware
functions.doc:
ProfilingMiddleware logs detailed timing info including handler execution and memory usage.
Reading memory stats briefly stops the whole program, so use it for development only.

functions.name: RateLimit
functions.doc:
RateLimit returns a middleware allowing each client limit requests every per, by IP
address. Up to limit requests can arrive at once, so a page making several calls in
quick succession isn't refused. Extra requests get a 429 with a Retry-After header.

Limits are kept in memory, so with several instances of your app behind a load
balancer, each one counts separately. Behind a proxy, every request appears to come
from the proxy's address; see RateLimitConfig.KeyFunc for that case.

Example:

	app.Use(middleware.RateLimit(100, time.Minute))
	app.UseIf(middleware.RateLimit(5, time.Minute), "/auth/login")
functions.code: func RateLimit(limit int, per time.Duration) Middleware

functions.name: RateLimitWithConfig
functions.doc:
RateLimitWithConfig returns a rate limiting middleware with a custom configuration.
It panics if the configuration can't work, so the mistake shows up at startup.

Behind a load balancer or proxy, set KeyFunc to read the client's address from the
header your proxy sets. Never trust that header without a proxy in front: clients can
set it to anything, and a new value on every request would never be limited.

Every response carries RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset
headers, so clients can slow down before they're refused.

functions.name: Recovery
functions.doc:
Panic Recovery
Recovery returns a middleware that recovers from panics and responds with a 500.
The panic and its stack trace are always logged, but the client only sees the panic
message in debug mode. http.ErrAbortHandler passes through, because it's how a handler
deliberately aborts a connection.

functions.name: ValidationMiddleware
functions.doc:
ValidationMiddleware returns a middleware that injects a validator instance into the Context.
The validator can then be accessed in handlers via c.Validator() (or c.SetValidator internally).
Example usage:

	app.Use(ValidationMiddleware(ValidationConfig{}))

functions.name: NewValidator
functions.doc:
NewValidator creates a validator that reports fields by their json name. A custom
validator passed to c.SetValidator needs the same setup to report the same names.

functions.name: NewContext
functions.doc: NewContext creates a Context for a server to pool, with room for a typical number of params.

functions.name: NewHTTPError
functions.doc: NewHTTPError creates an HTTPError. An empty message means the standard text for the code.

functions.name: NewRouter
functions.doc: NewRouter creates and returns a new Router instance.

functions.name: DefaultSettings
functions.doc: DefaultSettings returns the settings a server starts with.

functions.name: NewTemplateRenderer
functions.doc:
NewTemplateRenderer parses every template under dir.
Example: NewTemplateRenderer("views", nil)
functions.code: func NewTemplateRenderer(dir string, funcs template.FuncMap) (*TemplateRenderer, error)

functions.name: NewTemplateRendererFS
functions.doc:
NewTemplateRendererFS parses every template in fsys. Use it with embed.FS to
ship templates inside the binary, using fs.Sub if they're in a subfolder.
functions.code: func NewTemplateRendererFS(fsys fs.FS, funcs template.FuncMap) (*TemplateRenderer, error)
